# Branch A provisional HCC proposal

## Scientific opening and claim boundary

The clinically consequential question is whether the trajectory of postoperative liver function and synthetic reserve after hepatectomy contains information about subsequent HCC recurrence that is not captured by baseline tumor burden and the immediate postoperative state. The leading explanation is ordered recovery failure: persistent or worsening synthetic impairment after resection may mark a vulnerable remnant and/or ongoing tumor biology. A materially different rival is surveillance/selection artifact: postoperative labs and imaging are more often obtained for symptomatic or high-risk patients, so trajectory may proxy care intensity. A third rival is residual tumor severity: preoperative stage, size, vascular invasion, and pathology may explain both trajectory and recurrence.

The available evidence currently supports only that the HCC snapshot contains longitudinal encounter dates, procedures, diagnoses, labs, examination reports, medications, and pathology text linked by patient/encounter identifiers. It does not establish the hypothesis. The unresolved claim is:

Among patients with HCC who undergo hepatic resection and have at least one postoperative surveillance encounter, a prespecified postoperative liver-function trajectory (especially persistent/worsening synthetic reserve) predicts radiology- or diagnosis-documented HCC recurrence within 2 years beyond baseline tumor/pathology and immediate postoperative status.

This is an association/risk-stratification claim, not a causal or mechanistic claim.

## Exact data binding and verified availability

All joins stay inside HCC using documented keys 患者主索引 and 就诊号; no cross-dataset join is allowed. Snapshot: 3f97e661e1884c34c1e2cdbf74ba0cf6d6c8995853e85f1857c3d72b82ccf521.

- encounters, HCC/data_基本信息_2500296761891079109.csv: 患者主索引, 就诊号, 年龄, 性别, 就诊时间, 入院时间, 出院时间, 就诊科室. Use dates for chronology and windows.
- procedures, HCC/data_手术_8024330590283626027.csv: 患者主索引, 就诊号, 手术, 开始时间, 结束时间, 手术来源. Use 开始时间 and 手术 text to identify hepatic resection; ambiguous terms require review.
- diagnoses, HCC/data_诊断_7504718184492840569.csv: 患者主索引, 就诊号, 诊断名称, 诊断类型. Use HCC/recurrence labels; inherit encounter date from encounters.诊断时间 is unavailable.
- labs, HCC/data_检验_609065997844652188.csv: 患者主索引, 就诊号, 检验, 定性结果, 定量结果, 标本类型, 检验时间. Use prespecified liver/synthetic assays (albumin, bilirubin, INR/PT if present, AST/ALT, platelet count). Do not pool incompatible units; catalog says numeric labs lack a separate unit column.
- examinations, HCC/data_检查_4203595081195465282.csv: 患者主索引, 就诊号, 检查, 检查所见, 检查诊断, 开始时间, 机器型号, 检查号. Use 开始时间 and report text for surveillance and recurrence evidence; clean narrative HTML and adjudicate ambiguity.
- medications, HCC/data_用药_5693407050835159466.csv: 患者主索引, 就诊号, 用药, 单次用药计量, 单次用药计量单位, 频次, 开始时间, 结束时间, 用药方式, 药品类型. Use postoperative treatment exposure as time-varying covariate/sensitivity analysis, not treatment effect.
- pathology, HCC/data_病理_3292603985559017792.csv: 患者主索引, 就诊号, 病理, 检查所见, 检查诊断, 机器型号. Use pathology at/before index encounter; timing is inherited from encounter because pathology has no temporal column.
- clinical_documents, HCC/data_病历文书_8434587325530196878.csv: 患者主索引, 就诊号, 入院诊断, 入院诊断__duplicate_2, 诊疗经过, 出院情况, 出院诊断, 手术名称, 手术经过. Support index/recurrence adjudication only with explicit review rules; lexical flags are not validated diagnoses.
- vitals, transfers, and front_page are identifier-only and are not clinical inputs. orders is available but not needed for the primary estimand.

## Population and temporal design

Index population: HCC patients with a hepatic resection procedure, an HCC diagnosis in the linked encounter or a prespecified adjudication rule, and at least one postoperative encounter. Select the first qualifying resection per patient. Require at least one postoperative lab in days 0–30 for the primary analysis; retain complete-case and missingness sensitivity analyses.

Index time is resection 开始时间. Primary prediction window: postoperative days 0–30, secondary days 31–90. Follow-up for recurrence: days 0–730, primary horizon 2 years. Recurrence is a composite endpoint defined before fitting: new HCC recurrence diagnosis in diagnoses or recurrence-compatible examination report in examinations after index date, with manual adjudication for ambiguous reports. It is not a medication or encounter count.

Primary estimand: 2-year risk difference and risk ratio for recurrence between worsening/persistent impairment and recovering trajectories, adjusted for baseline age, sex, resection type, preoperative tumor/pathology features, preoperative labs, and immediate postoperative state. Freeze trajectory classification before outcome inspection. Secondary estimand: incremental predictive value over baseline, using time-dependent patient-level cross-validation and calibration.

## Baseline versus substantive alternative

Simple baseline: prespecified landmark logistic/Cox model using only baseline and immediate postoperative information: age, sex, resection type, preoperative HCC stage/pathology indicators, preoperative and day 0–7 labs, and immediate postoperative complications if documented. It tests whether the usual clinical snapshot is adequate and is auditable.

Substantive alternative: a time-varying trajectory model on the same patients and endpoint. For each prespecified assay, fit a robust longitudinal representation over days 0–90 (low-dimensional functional/latent trajectory or carefully regularized sequence model), then combine slope, nadir, persistence, and uncertainty with baseline covariates. The target is the same 2-year recurrence endpoint. The alternative can reveal direction and persistence of recovery, distinct recovery patterns, and whether sparse-measurement uncertainty changes risk; the baseline loses ordering, persistence, and patient-specific trajectory shape.

The alternative is scientifically useful only if it identifies a reproducible, interpretable trajectory pattern and improves held-out discrimination/calibration or decision-curve performance beyond baseline. A neural sequence model is optional; a low-dimensional functional model is preferable if lab density is sparse. Future solver: patient-level splits, no outcome leakage, nested tuning, bootstrap/repeated cross-validation uncertainty, and calibration plots. CPU is sufficient for cohort construction and baseline; one GPU is optional for a bounded sequence model after a measured feasibility probe. Discovery diagnostics are separate from the future solver envelope.

## Falsification and interpretation

Supportive: trajectory group/features remain associated with recurrence after baseline adjustment, are directionally consistent in held-out patients, improve calibration/discrimination, and are not confined to patients with more surveillance. This supports risk stratification and prospective validation, not causality or mechanism.

Adverse: no reproducible incremental signal, or signal disappears after accounting for surveillance intensity, baseline stage, and immediate postoperative state. This argues against trajectory as a useful discriminator and redirects attention to baseline severity or measurement practice.

Inconclusive: too few resection patients/events, missing units/assay coverage, ambiguous recurrence labels, or wide uncertainty. This does not refute the hypothesis and requires better adjudication, more complete longitudinal data, or a larger cohort.

Stronger claims require validated recurrence adjudication, reliable tumor size/vascular invasion/pathology details, treatment intent/response, imaging modality/timing, and external validation. Clinical experts must adjudicate ambiguous resection and recurrence labels. No treatment recommendation follows from this observational experiment.

## Current status and next deliverable

A managed row-availability census is running over exact HCC source files. The proposal is provisional until that census confirms event/assay support and three closest inspected works are attached with frozen receipts. The actual scientific deliverable is a fitted baseline and trajectory alternative on a frozen patient-level split, with held-out recurrence risk, calibration, uncertainty, and a prespecified adjudication table; readiness checks are not a scientific result.

# MerTK-positive macrophage exposure and donor-paired FLS reprogramming

## Scientific opening and hypothesis

The strongest available evidence is that MerTK-positive synovial tissue macrophages are associated with remission-associated states and can induce repair-like responses in synovial fibroblasts [K1]. A separate abstract supports directional macrophage-to-fibroblast communication through an EGF-receptor-dependent inflammatory axis [K2]. However, tissue heterogeneity, donor and treatment differences, and composition effects remain serious alternatives [K3]. The unresolved claim is narrower and falsifiable:

> In the same RA fibroblast-like synoviocyte (FLS) donor, exposure to MerTK/CD206-positive macrophages induces a reproducible repair-associated transcriptional shift relative to MerTK/CD206-negative macrophages and FLS-only controls, and at least a prespecified subset of that shift is attenuated when MerTK activity is inhibited.

This is a hypothesis about an ex vivo directional response, not proof that MerTK signaling causes remission in patients. Resolving it matters because a reproducible, perturbable FLS response would justify targeted validation of a macrophage-to-stroma mechanism; a null or inhibitor-insensitive result would redirect attention toward macrophage composition, disease state, or indirect effects.

## Population, temporal boundary, and variables

Primary analysis population: all 33 recorded FLS/coculture samples in E-MTAB-8873, with the biological unit treated as the donor/condition cluster rather than 33 independent donors. The design metadata explicitly marks most samples as requiring a contributing-donor model. The experiment is an ex vivo 48-hour comparison; no longitudinal patient outcome is available.

Join key: `sample_id` in `E-MTAB-8873.design.json` to the corresponding column in `E-MTAB-8873.counts.tsv.gz`. Required metadata fields are `sample_id`, `donor_id`, `donor_status`, `other_donor_id`, `age`, `sex`, `tissue`, `cell_type`, `condition`, `treatment`, and `cells`. The matrix has 445 measured feature rows and 33 sample columns; preserve source feature identifiers, including transcript/version suffixes, and do not infer unmeasured genes.

Primary contrasts are defined only where the same FLS donor has comparable conditions:
- Mpos versus Mneg, using samples whose condition names identify MerTK/CD206-positive versus MerTK/CD206-negative macrophages;
- Mpos versus FLS-only, using the corresponding FLS-only control;
- Mpos versus Mpos+MerTK inhibitor, using the explicit inhibitor/preInhibitor treatment labels;
- Mneg versus Mneg+LPS as a positive inflammatory control, and FLS-only versus FLS+inhibitor as an assay-control comparison where available.

The exact eligible pairs are determined from the frozen design file before looking at expression. Mixed macrophage ratios (1:3 and 3:1) are a secondary dose-response exploratory analysis, not independent donors. LPS and inhibitor samples are not used to define the primary Mpos/Mneg effect.

## Outcomes and analysis

The outcome is the log2 fold change in each measured feature, with a prespecified repair-associated summary based on the intersection of the targeted panel and the study's stated repair markers (COL1A1/COL1A2, TGFBI/TGFB3, and other panel members only if their identifiers are verified in the feature map). The primary estimand is the donor-cluster mean contrast with uncertainty from a mixed-effects or hierarchical model that groups repeated samples by FLS donor and contributing macrophage donor; no ordinary donor t-test is permitted. If the dependency structure is too sparse for a stable random-effects estimate, report a donor-level paired summary with a bootstrap or permutation distribution conditional on donor, and label the result exploratory.

The simple baseline is a fixed, biologically interpretable pathway score: the mean of prespecified repair-associated features, computed after log transformation and sample-size normalization, with the Mpos-Mneg and Mpos-only contrasts. It is transparent and directly tests the stated mechanism.

The substantive alternative is a regularized multivariate response model (for example, elastic-net or a low-rank functional model) fitted within donor groups to predict the condition contrast from all 445 measured features, with donor-clustered cross-validation and a held-out donor/condition split. It can reveal coordinated gene programs and whether the repair signal is distributed across the panel rather than concentrated in a few markers; the baseline loses that structure. The learned model is not selected for a small predictive gain. It is retained only if it improves held-out reconstruction of the condition contrast or identifies a stable, interpretable program that the fixed score misses. A mechanistic alternative, a ligand-receptor/state interaction model, is deferred because the admitted data do not provide a complete macrophage transcriptome or validated ligand measurements for this assay.

## Falsification and interpretation

Supportive results require: (1) a reproducible Mpos-versus-Mneg repair shift in the primary donor-clustered analysis; (2) attenuation of that shift in the explicit MerTK-inhibitor contrast; (3) concordant direction in at least two independent FLS donor clusters; and (4) no comparable shift in the FLS-only/inhibitor control. The learned model must reproduce the fixed-score direction on held-out donors.

Adverse results include a reproducible Mpos/Mneg difference that is not attenuated by MerTK inhibition, a shift confined to one donor or batch, or an inflammatory rather than repair pattern. These would weaken the proposed MerTK-specific directional mechanism but could support a different macrophage-state effect. Inconclusive results include wide uncertainty, insufficient paired donors, failed feature-map resolution, or conflicting fixed and learned summaries; they justify a new assay or additional donors rather than a mechanistic conclusion.

Computationally checkable claims are the matrix joins, feature counts, contrast definitions, model fits, uncertainty, and held-out behavior. Clinical remission, joint destruction, direct target engagement, and patient-level treatment benefit require clinical adjudication, longitudinal outcomes, protein/phospho-MerTK or ligand measurements, and an independent perturbation study.

## Exact data bindings and limitations

Read-only source paths:
- `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8873.counts.tsv.gz` (445 feature rows; 33 sample columns; SHA-256 `d218d3c46b652d533673c9ffc7876585bc51a39371f036e92d3ce568f28a4c0f`)
- `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8873.design.json` (sample metadata and condition/treatment fields; SHA-256 `fd2ae05bd0e31a8ba72454b97e22a48f5e53c179370e5f4b5343f5382b217ae4`)
- `[private-path]/repository.json` (study/protocol provenance; SHA-256 `75b17dd073e6e7fcb3390ca0314544e13ecf9fb249824ed7c1c718ca0a1da3ad`)
- `[private-path]/assay-registry.json` (verified assay limits; SHA-256 `e959459a88b18aea363570ed029a60199b4415e2fce7ab113bd1a31c77b7f70f`)

E-MTAB-8316 is a secondary whole-transcriptome context/control, not pooled with E-MTAB-8873:
- `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8316.counts.tsv.gz` (58,302 features; 12 samples; SHA-256 `9ceb4b7cf3d52d7f6e3800c827d491b174b646826fae9c6d1433c5d64b219645`)
- `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8316.design.json` (12 samples, four FLS donors, six nested monocyte donors; SHA-256 `ca011580853bbea30b4f68f21bb5b017721c3e47bfefee6e9083b44da04c4c81`)
- `[private-path]/repository.json` (protocol provenance; SHA-256 `3776aa1a4e7edef65c381bf5fce30ed31470ae6d3dbcc62fe1fe9f20505a16c1`)

E-MTAB-8322 is not used to claim whole-tissue composition: its pseudobulk contains measured macrophages only. GSE95588 is not used for donor-level inference because its column-to-GSM/donor mapping is unresolved and reused GSE57723 samples are not independent validation. No cross-dataset identity join is made.

## Deliverable and compute

The solver must newly fit the donor-clustered contrasts and both models, produce a feature-level contrast table, pathway-score table, uncertainty intervals, held-out donor evaluation, and a machine-readable conclusion classified as supportive, adverse, or inconclusive. Completion requires these outputs plus a report linking every conclusion to computed values. A CPU implementation is expected to be sufficient for 445 features and 33 samples; the future solver envelope is 16 CPUs, 262,144 MiB, 2 GPUs, and 28,800 seconds, but no GPU is required for this planned tabular analysis. The discovery episode did not execute the full study.

## Demonstration dispositions

The longitudinal EHR demonstrations are not adapted because this island has no patient-level dated EHR trajectories or outcomes; their methods do not answer this molecular communication question. The cancer multimodal demonstration is not adapted because the required images and complete STAR Methods are unavailable, and its lab-only adaptation would not resolve the present macrophage-to-FLS uncertainty. These are methodological context, not evidence for or against the hypothesis.

# Weight loss during HbA1c worsening as a near-term pancreatic-cancer signal

## Unresolved question and clinical importance
The strongest inspected evidence supports an association between recent-onset diabetes/worsening glycemia and weight loss with subsequent pancreatic cancer, but it does not establish whether this phenotype is specific to a near-term occult-cancer window in an unselected population, or whether it is explained by treatment, obesity-related metabolic deterioration, or another catabolic illness [K1][K2][K3]. Resolving this matters because a reproducible, temporally specific phenotype could justify expert review of targeted pancreatic evaluation, while a null or treatment-driven result would argue against indiscriminate imaging.

## Hypothesis
Among UK Biobank participants with two dated assessment visits, no pancreatic cancer before the later visit, and comparable change in HbA1c, clinically meaningful weight loss is associated with higher incidence of pancreatic cancer diagnosed within 2 years after the later visit than stable/increasing weight. The HbA1c-worsening × weight-loss interaction will be stronger in the 0–2-year window than in the 2–5-year window.

## Population, index and outcomes
Use only the UKB/ukb672073 identifier namespace and join on eid. Include adults with nonmissing HbA1c and weight at two assessment-center dates, a positive pre-specified interval (initially 1–10 years), and no ICD-10 C25 diagnosis before the later date. The index is the later assessment date. Primary outcome is first C25 diagnosis in 0–2 years; secondary outcome is 2–5 years. Censor at death or the fixed administrative end available in the frozen catalog. Use a landmark design; no post-index measurement is a predictor.

## Exact data bindings
- Assessment dates and weight/BMI: ukb672073_Assessment_Center.csv, Parquet source ukb_d61ec821b81b9034_parquet, key eid, columns 53-0.0–53-3.0, 21002-0.0–21002-3.0, and 21001-0.0–21001-3.0.
- HbA1c/glucose: ukb672073_Biological_Samples.csv, Parquet source ukb_a19465be8f90accc_parquet, key eid, columns 30750-0.0, 30750-1.0, 30740-0.0, 30740-1.0.
- Cancer/death: ukb672073_Health_Related_Outcomes.csv, Parquet source ukb_e53f1b242ccf9047_parquet, key eid, columns 40005-* and 40006-* for cancer dates/types, 40000-* for death, and 41270-*/41280-* as supplementary diagnosis checks.
- Recorded treatment/confounding: 20003-* columns in the same UKB assessment-center/health-outcome tables where present, plus available covariates. These are recorded codes, not a complete prescription history.
Do not join Olink (n_eid) or ukb671626 namespaces. Missing values are not zero.

## Analysis and method comparison
Primary model: cause-specific discrete-time or Cox model for 0–2-year C25 with HbA1c change, weight change, their interaction, age, sex, BMI, glucose, interval and recorded diabetes treatment; report interaction, absolute risk difference, calibration and robust uncertainty. Sensitivities use treatment-naive participants, stricter intervals, missingness indicators/inverse weighting, and the later window.

Baseline: the prespecified additive/interaction model above. Substantive alternative: a regularized latent longitudinal trajectory model (or mechanistic joint model if event support permits) using the same two dated HbA1c/glucose/weight observations, assessment timing, covariates and outcome, with patient-level time-dependent splits. It can reveal whether trajectory shape/timing carries information lost by two scalar changes, but cannot identify a mechanism. Compare on identical held-out participants using calibration, discrimination and uncertainty; do not select for a tiny predictive gain. CPU is appropriate for the baseline; the alternative is planned within the solver envelope (16 CPUs, 262,144 MiB, 2 GPUs, 28,800 seconds), with GPU use optional and unverified until a bounded fit.

## Falsification and interpretation
Supportive: reproducible positive interaction and excess near-term risk in held-out data, weaker later-window association, and stability under treatment/interval/missingness analyses. Adverse: no interaction, later-window-only association, or attenuation after treatment/missingness controls, favoring treatment, ascertainment or general catabolic explanations. Inconclusive: too few C25 events, sparse joint measurements, or wide confidence intervals; do not broaden to all cancers. A positive result establishes an association/prognostic pattern, not causality or a pancreatic mechanism. Complete prescriptions, symptoms, imaging, clinical adjudication and external validation are required for stronger claims.

## Demonstration dispositions
Delphi: a dated disease-history transformer is not needed for this narrow two-visit question; the trajectory model is the substantive alternative. ALADYNOULLI: the genetic longitudinal analysis is not reproduced because verified genetic linkage is not part of this design; an EHR/biomarker trajectory adaptation is explicitly different. Oncoformer: images and the full main text/STAR Methods are unavailable, so no multimodal reproduction is claimed; only verified UKB tables are used.

## Key references
[K1] Yuan et al., 2020, DOI 10.1001/jamaoncol.2020.2948 (abstract inspected).
[K2] Masamune et al., 2026, DOI 10.3390/cancers18182995 (abstract inspected).
[K3] Huang et al., 2026, DOI 10.1002/dmrr.70205 (abstract inspected).
